Amstrow is a company based in Dublin, Ireland, listed by Crunchbase under financial services and management. The short description says it offers corporate services and aviation support, which suggests a business-services or aircraft-related provider, though the detail is cut off in the source. Crunchbase shows about $190 million in total funding, with the latest round on 13 February 2023. Customers, ownership and scale are not clear from the available data, and the brand looks to have little consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Apollo GraphQL builds developer tools around GraphQL, the API query language: the open-source Apollo Client and Server, Apollo Federation, and the GraphOS platform for building and running a unified API layer. Customers are software engineering teams at enterprises and tech companies, paying for subscriptions and enterprise licences. Founded in 2012 as Meteor Development Group and headquartered in San Francisco, it has raised roughly $183 million, including a $130 million Series D in 2022. Privately held. Well known among developers, but B2B with almost no mainstream consumer recognition.

Arc is a San Francisco fintech offering a cash management and capital markets platform, aimed mainly at startups and growth companies that want to manage treasury balances, banking and financing in one place. It earns money from fees, interest spread and financing products. Crunchbase shows about $181 million raised in total, with the latest round in August 2022. Privately held. Brand awareness is limited to startup and venture circles, so it is a B2B name with little consumer visibility.

AsiaInfo is a Beijing-based software and IT services provider, best known for telecom software: billing, customer management, network operations and big-data and AI solutions for China's major carriers (China Mobile, China Unicom, China Telecom) and operators abroad. Revenue comes from software licences, projects and services. It was once Nasdaq-listed as AsiaInfo-Linkage, taken private in 2014, and is now listed in Hong Kong as AsiaInfo Technologies (1675.HK). Employs several thousand staff. Strictly B2B, with little consumer brand awareness outside telecom circles.

B-Soft is a software company based in Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China. Crunchbase lists it under developer platform and enterprise software, and describes it as an organisation focused on software, though the rest is cut off. It is shown with about CN¥1.24 billion in total funding, with the most recent round in May 2022. Its products, customers and ownership cannot be confirmed from the data available, and it appears to be a B2B firm with little public brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Barstool Sports is a US digital media company built around sports, pop culture and comedy, founded in Boston in 2003 by Dave Portnoy. It runs podcasts (Pardon My Take, Spittin' Chiclets), social channels, live events and a merchandise and apparel line, earning from advertising, sponsorship and merch. Based in New York, with a very large young male following. Penn Entertainment bought it in stages from 2020 and sold it back to Portnoy in 2023; Penn's sportsbook later became ESPN Bet. Highly visible consumer media brand.

BLEND is a London-based property development finance lender, providing loans to UK developers and property investors, typically for acquisition and construction projects, and earning money from interest and fees. Crunchbase lists it with about 140 million in funding, with the latest round in April 2022, which suggests the money is mainly debt facilities used to fund the loan book. Privately held. It is a specialist B2B lender with little public brand awareness beyond the property finance industry.

CHEQ is a go-to-market security company that protects digital advertising and marketing from bots, fake users, invalid traffic and fraud. Its products cover ad verification, onsite and conversion protection and audience security, sold to marketers, agencies and enterprise brands; it says it is trusted by 15,000 brands. Revenue is from software subscriptions. Founded in Israel, with its headquarters in New York, and backed by about $182 million in funding. Privately held. B2B, with some recognition among marketing and advertising professionals but little among consumers.

CleverTap is an all-in-one customer engagement and retention platform for mobile apps and websites, covering analytics, segmentation and messaging by push, email, SMS and WhatsApp, with AI-driven personalisation. Customers are consumer brands and apps (it claims thousands of clients in dozens of countries), paying subscription fees. Founded in Mumbai in 2013, now headquartered in San Francisco, and backed by investors including Sequoia, Tiger Global and CDPQ, with about $182 million raised. Privately held. B2B software with little consumer awareness.

CommerceIQ is a retail commerce management platform used by consumer goods brands to automate and optimise their e-commerce business on Amazon, Walmart and other retailers: pricing, advertising, supply chain, content and sales analytics, increasingly with AI. It says it powers 2,200+ brands and is paid through software subscriptions. Founded in 2014 and headquartered in Mountain View, California, with a large engineering team in Bangalore, and about $195 million raised (SoftBank-backed, among others). Privately held. B2B, known within CPG and e-commerce circles but not by consumers.

CorPower Ocean is a Swedish wave energy developer that makes compact floating buoys, using its patented phase-control technology, to turn ocean waves into electricity. Customers are utilities and project developers for offshore energy, and it works on pilot projects in Portugal, Scotland and Norway. Revenue is from technology and project deals plus public grants. Based in the Stockholm area (Hagersten), formed in 2009 according to Crunchbase, with a funding round of about 162 million in May 2026 that lifts its total raised. Privately held. Pure B2B cleantech with little consumer awareness.

Culture Trip is a London-based travel company that started as a digital media site publishing travel and culture articles and later moved into curated small-group trips. Crunchbase describes premium small-group adventures for like-minded travellers. It sells trips directly to consumers, mainly young adults, and earlier made money from advertising and partnerships. Founded in 2011, it has raised about $185 million, with the latest round shown in August 2020. Privately held. Moderate consumer awareness, especially among younger travellers online.

Gloat is a workforce agility and talent marketplace platform that uses AI to match employees with internal jobs, projects, gigs and mentors, and to plan skills. Customers are large enterprises, such as global manufacturers and consumer groups, paying subscription fees. Founded in Israel and now headquartered in New York, it has raised about $182 million, with its latest round in June 2022. Privately held. B2B HR software, known among HR leaders but with little consumer brand awareness.

Immersive (formerly Immersive Labs) is a Bristol-based cyber security company whose platform measures and builds cyber readiness through hands-on exercises, simulations and crisis drills for security teams, developers and executives. Customers include large enterprises, financial firms and government bodies, paying subscription fees. Founded in 2017 and backed by investors including Insight Partners and Goldman Sachs, it has raised about $190 million, including a $75 million Series C in 2022. Privately held, with offices in the UK and US. B2B, little consumer brand awareness.

Jushuitan Network Technology is a Shanghai-based provider of e-commerce SaaS and ERP software, used by online sellers in China to manage orders, inventory, warehouses and multi-platform stores on marketplaces such as Taobao, Tmall and JD. Revenue comes from software subscriptions and related services. Crunchbase shows about $191 million raised in total, with the latest round in June 2020. Privately held. B2B software with a large base of small online merchants but almost no consumer awareness.

Koalafi is a Washington, DC based fintech offering omnichannel financial products, such as lease-to-own and consumer financing, that help retailers sell to shoppers who may not qualify for conventional credit, at the point of sale in stores and online. Merchants in categories like furniture, mattresses and automotive offer it to customers; it earns from fees and finance income. Crunchbase shows about $195 million raised, with the latest round in August 2022. Privately held. B2B2C, with low consumer brand awareness.

LeadSquared is a sales execution and marketing automation platform, a CRM used to capture, nurture and convert leads, particularly in education, financial services, healthcare and real estate. It sells subscription software to enterprises and mid-sized firms, mostly in India, the Middle East, Southeast Asia and the US. Founded in 2009 and based in Bengaluru, with about $188 million raised, including a Series C in mid-2022. Privately held. B2B, well known in the Indian software scene but with little consumer visibility.

Malwarebytes is a cybersecurity company known for its anti-malware software for Windows, Mac, Android and iOS, with products such as Malwarebytes Premium, Browser Guard and Privacy VPN, and ThreatDown endpoint protection for businesses. It sells to consumers and to small and mid-sized organisations through subscriptions. Founded in 2008 by Marcin Kleczynski, with offices in Santa Clara and Clearwater, Florida, plus Europe, it has raised about $180 million and is privately held. It serves tens of millions of users and has good consumer brand recognition for a security vendor.

Meican is a Beijing-based mobile ordering platform for workplace meals in China. Companies and employees use its app and website to order lunch and snacks from partner restaurants, with delivery to the office, and many employers subsidise the cost. It earns commissions and service fees from restaurants and corporate clients. Founded around 2010, it has raised about $190 million, with the latest round in December 2021. Privately held. Well known among white-collar workers in large Chinese cities, with little awareness outside China.

Modern Meadow is a biotechnology and materials company that develops bio-fabricated materials, using proteins such as collagen, for fashion, beauty and other industries. Its products include Bio-Vera, a collagen-based ingredient for skincare and cosmetics, and bio-based leather alternatives, which it licenses or supplies to brand partners. Founded in 2011, it is based in Pine Brook, New Jersey, and has raised about $184 million. Privately held. B2B, with brand recognition mostly in sustainable materials and fashion innovation circles; the end consumer rarely sees its name.

Modulr is a London-based payments company offering account and payments infrastructure through APIs, so that businesses and software platforms can embed payments, accounts and collections into their products. It is authorised by the UK's Financial Conduct Authority as an e-money institution, and serves fintechs, payroll and marketplace platforms and corporates. It earns on transaction fees and platform charges. Founded in 2015, it has raised about 145 million, including a Series C in 2022 led by General Atlantic. Privately held. B2B, little consumer awareness.

Muck Rack is a public relations management and media intelligence platform. Communications teams use it to find journalists, pitch stories, monitor news and social coverage, and report on PR results. It sells software subscriptions to brands, agencies and nonprofits and publishes industry research. Founded in 2009, it has raised about $180 million, notably a $100 million round led by Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs in 2022. Privately held, headquartered per Crunchbase in Miami, with roots in New York. B2B, well known to PR professionals but not to consumers.

Nexxiot is a Zurich-based TradeTech company that uses IoT sensors, connectivity and AI to track and monitor rail freight wagons, intermodal containers and trailers, with data on location, condition, utilisation and cargo. Customers are logistics operators, railways, shippers and wagon owners; revenue is from hardware plus software subscriptions. Backed by investors including Mitsubishi, DB and Swiss funds, it has raised about $184 million, with its latest round in May 2022. Privately held. Strictly B2B, with little public brand awareness.

Oakbrook Finance is a financial service provider based in Nottingham, England, and the short description says it specialises in lending, apparently to consumers needing short-term or small-sum credit. Crunchbase shows about 142 million in funding, with the latest round in March 2022, which probably reflects debt facilities that fund its loan book. Ownership, products and scale are not confirmed by the available data. Brand awareness among consumers is unclear. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Olo is a SaaS platform for restaurant digital ordering and delivery. Its Ordering, Dispatch, Rails and Engage products let chains such as Five Guys, Wingstop and Subway take online orders, handle third-party delivery, and run loyalty and marketing, with revenue from subscription and transaction fees. Based in New York and founded in 2005, it listed on the NYSE in 2021 (OLO) and was taken private by Thoma Bravo in a roughly $2 billion deal announced in 2025. Serves tens of thousands of restaurant locations. B2B, little consumer awareness.

OpenGov provides cloud software for the public sector: budgeting and planning, financial and ERP systems, permitting and licensing, procurement and asset management for cities, counties, states and schools. It sells subscriptions to thousands of US government agencies. Founded in 2012 and headquartered in San Francisco, it has raised roughly $178 million, with major backing from Cox Enterprises, which holds a controlling stake. Privately held. A B2G software brand, well known among public finance staff but with no consumer awareness.

OurCrowd is a Jerusalem-based equity crowdfunding and venture investing platform that lets accredited investors back startups and funds, mostly Israeli and global technology companies, alongside its own team. It earns management fees and carry on its funds and portfolio deals. Founded in 2013 by Jon Medved, it has invested in hundreds of companies and has raised about $197 million for itself. Privately held. Well known in the Israeli and global venture community, with limited recognition among general consumers.

Personetics supplies AI-driven personalisation and customer engagement software to banks, providing personal financial insights, budgeting nudges, savings guidance and self-service functions inside the bank's own app. Customers are large retail banks and financial institutions around the world, paying software and licence fees. Founded in 2010 with Israeli roots, it is headquartered in New York and has raised about $178 million, with a major round in early 2022. Privately held. Strictly B2B, with the end consumer seeing the bank's brand rather than its own.

SeekOut is a talent search and recruiting platform that uses AI to find and analyse candidates across public data sources, covering sourcing, diversity recruiting, security-cleared talent and internal talent mobility. Customers are corporate recruiting teams, staffing firms and government contractors, paying subscription fees. Founded in 2017 by Anoop Gupta and based in Bellevue, Washington, it has raised about $189 million, including a Series C in 2022. Privately held. B2B, known among recruiters and HR leaders but not among consumers.

SiteMinder is an Australian hotel software company offering a platform for hotel distribution and revenue growth: channel manager, booking engine, payments and demand-planning tools used by independent hotels, resorts and groups. It claims tens of thousands of properties in around 150 countries and earns from subscriptions and transaction fees. Founded in 2006 and based in Sydney, it listed on the ASX (SDR) in November 2021. B2B, well known in the hospitality sector but not among consumers.

Sitetracker is a SaaS platform, built on the Salesforce platform, for deploying, operating and maintaining infrastructure projects such as telecom networks, utilities, renewable energy assets and electric vehicle charging. It sells subscriptions to carriers, tower companies, utilities and developers who need to manage large portfolios of sites. Based in Montclair, New Jersey, it has raised about $183 million, including a 2022 round, and is privately held. Strictly B2B, with little brand awareness outside infrastructure and telecom.

Snowplus is a Chinese e-cigarette (vape) brand from Shenzhen, selling closed-system vaping devices and pods to adult consumers in China. It is listed under e-commerce and electronics in Crunchbase and has raised about $181 million, with the latest round in June 2020. Ownership details are not confirmed here. Consumer visibility is mainly within China's vaping market. For sponsorship, note that nicotine and tobacco-type brands face heavy advertising restrictions in most markets and in motorsport.

Stackline is a Seattle-based retail intelligence and software company giving consumer goods brands and retailers analytics on e-commerce performance, notably sales, share and pricing on Amazon, Walmart and other marketplaces, plus advertising and retail optimisation tools. It sells subscriptions to hundreds of brands and agencies. Founded in 2014, it has raised about $180 million and is privately held. Strictly B2B, with recognition in e-commerce and CPG circles but little among consumers.

Tiger Data, the company behind TimescaleDB, builds developer-focused database software on PostgreSQL for time-series, events, analytics and AI workloads, plus a managed cloud service. It was previously known as Timescale and rebranded to Tiger Data in 2025. Customers are software developers and engineering teams at companies handling IoT, financial, energy and application data; revenue comes from cloud subscriptions and enterprise support. Headquartered in New York and founded in 2017, it has raised about $181 million. Privately held. B2B, popular with developers but unknown to consumers.

Tricolor Holdings was a Texas-based auto lender and used-car seller serving mainly Hispanic and underbanked consumers, including borrowers with limited credit history who used individual taxpayer ID numbers. It originated subprime auto loans and funded them through asset-backed securities and bank credit lines. Based in Irving, Texas, it raised about $190 million in equity. Privately held. In September 2025 it filed for Chapter 7 liquidation amid fraud allegations. Brand awareness was regional and consumer-focused, now tainted by the collapse.

Turtlemint is an Indian insurtech marketplace that helps people and small businesses compare and buy motor, health, life and general insurance, mostly through a network of agents and advisors using its digital tools. It earns commissions from insurers. Founded in 2015 and based in Mumbai, it has raised about $197 million, with its latest round in April 2022. Privately held. Reasonable consumer and agent awareness in India, with little outside it.

Velvaere is a luxury ski-in, ski-out residential community in Park City, Utah, in the United States, categorised by Crunchbase under health care and real estate. It is a high-end resort real estate and lifestyle development rather than a technology firm, selling homes and residences to wealthy buyers. Crunchbase shows about $197 million in funding, with the latest round in December 2025. Ownership, scale and number of residences are not confirmed from the available data. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

ViaBill is a Copenhagen-based buy-now-pay-later payment option that lets online shoppers pay in full after 30 days or split purchases into instalments, offered at checkout by online merchants. It earns merchant fees and consumer charges and is available mainly in Denmark, other Nordic countries, the US and parts of Europe. Crunchbase shows about $177 million raised, with the latest round in February 2022. Privately held. Well recognised by shoppers in Denmark, but limited elsewhere.

Virtana is a Palo Alto-based software company whose hybrid cloud optimisation platform gives enterprises observability, capacity planning and cost optimisation across on-premises infrastructure and public clouds, with AI-driven analytics. It was formerly known for infrastructure performance monitoring under the earlier Virtual Instruments name. Customers are large enterprises and service providers, paying software subscriptions. Crunchbase shows about $195 million raised. Privately held. B2B, with little brand awareness beyond enterprise IT.

Zappi is a market research technology company whose automated consumer insights platform lets brands test ads, concepts, products and innovations with consumers through surveys and AI-driven analysis, with fast results. Customers include global consumer goods and media brands, which pay platform subscriptions. Originating in the UK and now headquartered in Boston, it has raised about $194 million, with a large round in late 2022. Privately held. B2B, known among brand marketers but not among consumers.

Zoovu is an AI product discovery platform that unifies search, guided selling, product recommendation and conversational tools for e-commerce and B2B sellers, helping shoppers find the right product. Customers are brands and retailers in sectors such as consumer electronics and manufacturing, paying software subscriptions. Founded in Austria in 2012 and now headquartered in Boston, it has raised about $188 million, with a round in June 2022. Privately held. B2B, with little consumer awareness beyond the stores that embed it.

Aisera is a Santa Clara, California software company whose agentic AI platform automates enterprise service across IT, HR, customer support and sales, using AI agents and assistants that resolve requests and run workflows. Customers are large enterprises, which pay software subscriptions. Founded in 2017, it has raised about $164 million, with its latest round in August 2022. Privately held. Strictly B2B, with recognition in enterprise IT and service management circles but no consumer awareness.

AngelList is a San Francisco platform that connects startups with investors and talent. Its products include AngelList Venture, which provides fund and syndicate administration for venture capital managers, and the Wellfound job marketplace for startup roles (previously AngelList Talent). It earns fees on funds and subscriptions. Founded in 2010 by Naval Ravikant and Babak Nivi, it has raised about $170 million and is privately held. Very well known in the startup and venture world, with limited recognition among general consumers.

Camino Financial is a Los Angeles online lender focused on small businesses owned by Latino entrepreneurs in the United States, offering loans and credit-building help, often to borrowers underserved by traditional banks, using data-driven underwriting. It earns interest and fees. Crunchbase shows about $170 million in total funding, much of it debt facilities, with the latest round in April 2022. Privately held. Community-focused consumer and small-business brand, known mainly within the Latino small-business community in California.

CaptivateIQ is a San Francisco SaaS company that makes sales compensation and commission management software, so finance and sales operations teams can calculate, model and pay commissions without spreadsheets. Customers are mid-size and enterprise companies, especially in software and technology, paying subscriptions. Founded in 2017, it has raised about $165 million, including a Series C in early 2022 backed by Accel and Sequoia. Privately held. B2B, known in sales operations and finance teams but not among consumers.

Centauro is a Brazilian multichannel sports retailer with a large chain of physical stores plus a major e-commerce site, selling sportswear, footwear and equipment from brands such as Nike and adidas along with private labels. It sells to consumers across Brazil and earns from retail margins. Based in Sao Paulo, it is the main brand of Grupo SBF, listed on the B3 exchange (SBFG3) since an IPO in 2020 that raised about R$900 million. Strong consumer brand within Brazil, with no presence abroad.

Codat is a London-based company providing an API that connects financial software, banks and lenders to small businesses' accounting, commerce and banking data, and it builds embedded finance products on that data. Customers are fintechs, banks, software platforms and lenders, paying platform fees. Founded in 2017, it has raised about $177 million, with a Series C in mid-2022. Privately held. B2B, well known in fintech and developer circles but with no consumer brand awareness.

Connectivity Wireless Solutions is a company based in Duluth, Georgia, in the United States, categorised by Crunchbase as mobile. The short description calls it a leading nationwide provider, apparently of wireless connectivity services, though the text is cut off. It is shown with about $170 million in total funding, with the latest round in March 2025. Customers, services, ownership and size cannot be confirmed from the available data, and it appears to be a B2B business with little consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Contentstack is an Austin-based provider of a composable digital experience platform: a headless content management system, plus tools for personalisation, automation and AI-assisted content delivery across websites, apps and devices. Customers are mid-size and large companies, including retail and media brands, which pay subscription fees. The business grew from Built.io, started in India, and has raised about $169 million, with backing from firms such as Insight Partners. Privately held. B2B, recognised in the web content and developer market but not by consumers.

Data Grand is a company based in Shanghai, China, which Crunchbase describes as a developer of semantic analysis solutions, in the natural language processing field. That suggests software for reading and extracting information from text and documents for business customers, but products and clients are not named in the source. It shows about CN¥1.07 billion in funding, with the latest round in March 2022. Ownership and scale are not confirmed, and the brand appears to be B2B with little public awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Deerma is a Chinese home appliance maker, based in Foshan, Guangdong, that designs and manufactures new-generation small household appliances, such as humidifiers, vacuum cleaners, steam mops and kitchen gadgets, sold through e-commerce platforms and retail channels, mostly in China. It earns product revenue from consumers. Crunchbase shows about CN¥1.21 billion raised, with the latest round in July 2020. Privately held. Reasonable consumer awareness in China's online appliance market, with little outside it.

Digital Diagnostics, formerly IDx, is a medical AI company in Coralville, Iowa. Its LumineticsCore (IDx-DR) system, in 2018, became the first FDA-authorised autonomous AI diagnostic, detecting diabetic retinopathy from retinal images without a clinician reading them. It sells to primary care clinics, health systems and payers, charging per-use and service fees. It has raised about $173 million and is privately held. Known in healthcare and AI circles, with no direct consumer awareness.

Eclairion is a French data computing centre in Bruyeres-le-Chatel, in the Essonne area south of Paris, offering high-performance computing and AI infrastructure hosting for public research bodies, industry and technology clients. It earns from hosting, capacity and service contracts. Crunchbase shows about 160 million in funding, with the latest round in February 2025, suggesting investment in capacity expansion. Privately held. B2B infrastructure with little brand awareness outside the HPC and data centre sector.

Founderpath is an Austin, Texas fintech that gives SaaS founders non-dilutive capital, in effect funding against their recurring revenue, so they can grow without selling equity. It also runs a founder community and learning programme. It earns fees and finance income from the capital it provides. Crunchbase shows about $161 million raised in total, largely debt-style financing, with the latest round in August 2022. Privately held. B2B, with a reputation in the SaaS startup scene and no consumer awareness.

Genvid Technologies is a New York software company providing a platform for massive interactive live events, where very large online audiences can influence the story or game via live video streams. It worked with Facebook Watch on the interactive series Rival Peak and on titles with game studios. It earns from technology licensing and project fees. Crunchbase shows about $166 million raised, with the latest round in July 2021. Privately held. B2B, known in gaming, esports and streaming circles.

HomeToGo is a Berlin-based marketplace for vacation rentals, aggregating millions of holiday homes and apartments from hundreds of partners on its metasearch brands, and it has also moved into direct supply via acquisitions such as Interhome. Travellers use it for free and it earns commissions and advertising fees. Founded in 2014, it listed via a SPAC in 2022 and trades in Frankfurt and on Nasdaq (HTG). Strong consumer awareness across Europe in the travel sector, under brands including HomeToGo and Interhome.

Inagora is an e-commerce company based in Tokyo, Japan, which Crunchbase describes as a site providing cross-border e-commerce. That suggests an online platform linking Japanese goods and sellers with overseas, probably Chinese, buyers, though the source text is cut off. It shows about $163 million in total funding, with the latest round in January 2020. Products, ownership and scale cannot be confirmed from the available data, so the brand's public visibility is unclear. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

LinkSquares is a Boston software company that makes an AI-powered contract lifecycle management platform, helping legal and finance teams store, search, analyse and track contracts, with tools for reviewing and extracting key terms. It sells subscriptions to mid-sized and large companies. Founded in 2015, it has raised about $161 million, with a Series C in 2022. Privately held. Strictly B2B, with recognition in legal technology but no consumer awareness.

Material Security is a San Francisco cyber security company that protects email and other cloud workspace content, such as Google Workspace and Microsoft 365, by detecting phishing and account takeovers and locking down sensitive messages and files after login. Customers are mid-size and large enterprises, which pay subscriptions. Founded in 2018 and backed by investors including Andreessen Horowitz and Kleiner Perkins, it has raised about $162 million. Privately held. B2B, known among security teams, not consumers.

NewStore is a Boston-based software company offering a cloud platform for omnichannel retail: mobile point of sale, clienteling, order management and fulfilment tools that let store staff sell and deliver across channels. Customers are fashion, luxury and department store brands, paying subscriptions. Founded in Germany in 2014, it has raised about $163 million, with its latest round in July 2021. Privately held. B2B, with recognition among retail technology buyers but almost none among shoppers.

NexHealth is a San Francisco healthcare technology company with a patient booking and communication platform, plus a developer API that synchronises data with practice management software, for dental, medical and other clinics. Practices pay subscriptions, and software partners use the API. Founded in 2017, it has raised about $177 million, including a 2022 Series C. Privately held. B2B, familiar to dental and clinic operators and health-tech developers, but patients rarely know the brand.

Olam is a Singapore-headquartered agri-business that sources, processes and supplies food ingredients, spices, vegetables, coffee, cocoa, edible nuts and other agricultural products, now organised mainly into ofi (Olam Food Ingredients) and Olam Agri. Crunchbase's text refers to its spices and vegetable ingredients business, including dehydrated onion. Customers are global food and beverage makers and traders. Founded in 1989, it operates across dozens of countries and is controlled by Temasek-linked shareholders and listed in Singapore. Mostly B2B, with limited consumer brand visibility.

Opera is an Oslo-based software company behind the Opera web browser, including the gaming browser Opera GX, Opera Mini, and Opera News, with a growing AI browser strategy. It serves hundreds of millions of monthly users worldwide and earns from search deals, advertising and fintech and gaming services. Its ADSs trade on Nasdaq (OPRA), with a Chinese-led shareholder group holding a controlling stake. It is active in esports and gaming sponsorship. Strong consumer awareness, especially among younger and gaming audiences.

Panzura is a data management company whose products give enterprises a global file system and hybrid cloud storage, enabling teams across multiple locations to access, protect and analyse unstructured data such as engineering and media files. Customers are large organisations in sectors like construction, engineering, media and government, paying software and subscription fees. Based in San Francisco, it has raised about $170 million. Privately held. B2B enterprise infrastructure, with little consumer awareness.

Pave is a San Francisco compensation platform that gives companies real-time pay benchmarking, equity and salary planning, and increasingly AI tools for HR and finance leaders, using live data from its customers' payroll and equity systems. Customers are startups and growth-stage technology companies, who pay subscriptions. Founded in 2019, it has raised about $163 million, including a 2022 Series C. Privately held. B2B, well known among HR and people teams but not among consumers.

Post Brothers is a Philadelphia real estate developer and housing operator, building and managing luxury residential apartment properties and mixed-use projects, with a focus on urban sites in cities such as Philadelphia and Dallas. It earns rents and development gains. Crunchbase shows about $170 million in funding, with the latest round in October 2025, likely equity or capital for projects. Privately held. Locally known in its property markets, but not a national consumer brand.

Proportunity is a financial services organisation based in London, England, which Crunchbase lists under artificial intelligence. The short description says it is made up of, apparently, a group of finance or property-related units, but the text is cut off. It shows about $168 million in total funding, with the latest round in May 2022. Products, customers, ownership and scale cannot be confirmed from the available data. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Qcells (Hanwha Qcells) is a major solar company making solar cells, modules and energy storage systems, and developing solar projects and home energy services. Its ingot-to-module factory in Georgia, USA, is among the largest in the country. It sells to utilities, installers, businesses and homeowners worldwide, earning from equipment and projects. Founded in Germany in 1999, it is now part of South Korea's Hanwha group, within Hanwha Solutions, with global sales offices. B2B2C brand with growing visibility in the US residential solar market.

Quanergy Systems was a San Jose, California maker of 3D solid-state LiDAR sensors and smart sensing software, used in security, smart city, transport and industrial automation as well as autonomous vehicles. It went public via a SPAC merger on the NYSE in early 2022 (QNGY) but filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in December 2022 and was delisted. It had raised about $165 million before listing. B2B, with low consumer awareness; it is effectively defunct as a sponsor prospect.

RStudio, now called Posit PBC after a 2022 renaming, builds open-source and commercial data science tools for the R and Python languages, including the RStudio IDE, Shiny, Posit Connect, Workbench and Package Manager. Customers are data scientists, analysts and enterprises such as pharma and financial firms, paying for professional licences and cloud services. It is a public benefit corporation based in Boston and has raised about $166 million. Widely used by programmers and statisticians, but unknown to the general public.

Sanctuary Wealth is a US wealth management platform that lets established financial advisers and teams run independent, branded firms with shared technology, custody, compliance and investment support, in a partnership model. Revenue comes from advisory fees on assets supported by the platform. Based in Indianapolis according to Crunchbase, with a wide national network, it shows about $175 million in funding, with a round in July 2022. Privately held. Known in the adviser community, with limited awareness among individual investors.

Solar Foods is a Finnish food technology company that produces Solein, a protein made from carbon dioxide, hydrogen and microbes, as an ingredient for foods and drinks. Its Factory 01 is in Vantaa, near Helsinki, with a larger Factory 02 planned, and it sells to food manufacturers and brand partners. Founded in 2017, it is listed on Nasdaq First North Growth Market Finland, and has raised about 166 million in funding. B2B ingredient brand with low consumer recognition but strong sustainability and media interest.

Sticky.io (formerly Limelight CRM) is a San Francisco company offering a subscription-focused billing, CRM and payment orchestration platform for e-commerce merchants, especially direct-to-consumer brands selling recurring products. Customers use it to manage subscriptions, retries, chargebacks and multiple payment processors, paying software and processing fees. Crunchbase shows about $165 million raised, with the latest round in June 2021. Privately held. B2B, mostly known to e-commerce operators, not consumers.

TCNS Clothing is an Indian women's fashion company behind brands such as W, Aurelia, Wishful, Elleven and Folklore, selling ethnic and western wear through exclusive brand outlets, large-format stores and online marketplaces across India. Based in New Delhi, it was listed on the NSE and BSE after a 2016 IPO. Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail agreed to acquire a controlling stake in 2023, completing in 2024. Strong consumer brands within India, with limited presence abroad.

Teleport is an Oakland, California infrastructure identity company, growing out of Gravitational and the open-source project, that secures access to servers, databases, Kubernetes clusters, cloud and internal apps with short-lived credentials, audit logging and zero-trust controls. Customers are engineering and security teams at enterprises and technology firms, paying subscriptions. It has raised about $169 million. Privately held. B2B, known among DevOps and security engineers but not by consumers.

Wakefit is a Bengaluru-based sleep and home solutions company selling mattresses, bed frames, sofas, furniture and home furnishings directly to Indian consumers, online and through its growing network of company-owned experience stores. It earns product revenue and is known for its direct-to-consumer model and heavy advertising. Founded in 2016, it has raised about $176 million from backers including Peak XV (Sequoia) and Verlinvest, with a December 2025 round shown by Crunchbase. Strong consumer awareness in India.

ZEGOCLOUD is a Singapore-headquartered provider of real-time communication software, offering video, voice and chat APIs and SDKs that developers embed into apps for live streaming, video calls, voice rooms, online classes and social features. Customers are app developers and companies in social, gaming, education, telehealth and e-commerce, paying usage-based fees. It grew out of China's ZEGO and has raised about $172 million, including a 2022 round. Privately held. B2B developer tool with little consumer awareness.

Zongteng Network is a Shenzhen-based provider of cross-border logistics and shipping services, helping Chinese e-commerce sellers ship goods to overseas buyers through warehousing, freight forwarding, last-mile delivery and related supply chain software. Customers are online merchants selling on marketplaces such as Amazon. Revenue comes from freight and service fees. Crunchbase shows about CN¥1.2 billion raised, with the latest round in July 2020. Privately held. B2B, with little consumer awareness.

Fortress Information Security is an Orlando-based cyber security company focused on supply chain risk for critical infrastructure, especially electric utilities and other operators. It assesses vendors, hardware and software components, and runs shared assessment programmes for utilities and government agencies, using AI-assisted tooling. It earns from subscriptions and services. Founded in 2018, it has raised about $160 million, including a 2022 investment. Privately held. B2B and B2G, known in utilities and national security circles, with no consumer awareness.

XVERSE Technology is a Shenzhen-based artificial intelligence and 3D company building large language models and generative AI, plus tools for creating virtual worlds, digital humans and 3D interactive content. It sells to businesses in gaming, entertainment, culture and tourism, and serves consumer apps on top of its models. Crunchbase shows about $160 million in funding, with the latest round in March 2022. Privately held. B2B, with some recognition in China's AI and metaverse sector.

36Kr is a Beijing-based Chinese technology and business media company covering startups, venture capital and innovation, running news sites and apps, events, and corporate services such as advertising, subscription content and consulting. It earns from advertising, enterprise services and events. Founded in 2010, it is listed on Nasdaq as 36Kr Holdings (KRKR), following a listing in 2019 and a funding total of about $153 million. Strong recognition among Chinese tech and investor audiences, with low awareness elsewhere.

Babycare is a Shanghai-based maternal and infant brand, selling baby products such as diapers, wet wipes, strollers, feeding items and children's clothing, mainly online in China through its own flagship stores on Tmall, Douyin and other platforms. It earns product revenue from parents. Crunchbase shows about CN¥1 billion raised, with the latest round in February 2021. Privately held. Strong consumer brand awareness among Chinese young parents, with limited presence abroad.

Bombas is a US direct-to-consumer apparel brand, started in 2013 by David Heath and Randy Goldberg, best known for comfort-focused socks, and now also underwear, t-shirts, slippers and sweaters. For every item sold it donates one to homeless shelters and community organisations, with well over 100 million items given. It sells mainly online and through selected retailers. Based in New York, it has raised about $150 million and is privately held. Strong consumer awareness in the US, driven by heavy digital marketing.

Budbee is a Stockholm-based last-mile delivery company, delivering online orders to consumers' homes, to parcel lockers and to pickup points across Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Finland, the Netherlands and Belgium. Retailers pay delivery fees, and consumers see the Budbee box and app. It was merged with Instabox in 2022 to form Instabee, a pan-Nordic logistics group backed by investors including Kinnevik. About $154 million raised. Good consumer recognition in the Nordics through its parcel boxes and delivery vans.

CJ 4DPLEX is the South Korean company behind 4DX, the multisensory cinema format with moving seats and effects such as wind, water, scents and fog, and ScreenX, a panoramic multi-screen format. Both are installed in hundreds of cinemas across dozens of countries, and it earns from equipment sales, installation and a share of ticket revenue. Based in Seoul, it is part of CJ CGV, under the CJ group. About 220 billion won in funding is recorded. Strong visibility among cinema-goers.

Coweta-Fayette EMC is a consumer-owned electric membership cooperative serving residential, commercial and industrial customers south and west of Atlanta, in Georgia, in the United States. It distributes electricity and offers related services such as energy efficiency programmes, and is owned by its members. Based in Palmetto, Georgia, it shows about $158 million in funding, with the latest round in December 2024. It is a utility with regional recognition among its members and no national brand presence.

Ellevest is a New York digital investing and financial planning platform created for women, founded in 2014 by Sallie Krawcheck, former Wall Street executive. It offers automated investment portfolios, retirement accounts, banking-style features and coaching, mostly directly to individual consumers, and earns subscription and advisory fees. It has raised about $152 million, with a 2022 round. Privately held. Reasonable consumer awareness in the US among women investors, supported by media coverage of its founder.

Evisort is an AI-powered contract intelligence and management platform, used by legal, procurement and sales teams to store, analyse, search and automate contracts using its own language models. It was founded in 2016 as a Harvard Law School spin-out and based in San Francisco, with about $156 million raised. Workday announced the acquisition of Evisort in September 2024, folding it into its enterprise software suite. B2B with strong recognition among legal technology buyers and none among consumers.

Finio Technology is a company based in Toronto, Ontario, Canada, categorised by Crunchbase under finance and financial services. The short description says it is committed to integrating the power of, apparently, technology into finance, but the text is cut off. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Customers, product range, ownership and scale cannot be confirmed from the available data. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

HackerOne is a San Francisco security company running a platform that connects organisations with a large community of ethical hackers for bug bounty programmes, vulnerability disclosure, penetration testing and continuous threat exposure management. Customers include technology firms, financial institutions and governments such as the US Department of Defense, paying platform and bounty fees. Founded in 2012, it has raised about $159 million. Privately held. Well known in the security industry, with little awareness among consumers.

Hexagon Composites is a Norwegian company, based in Alesund, making lightweight composite pressure cylinders and systems for storing and transporting compressed natural gas, biogas and hydrogen. Its businesses include Hexagon Agility, for natural gas fuel systems for trucks and buses, and Mobile Pipeline. Customers are vehicle makers, fleet operators and gas companies. It is listed on Euronext Oslo (HEX). B2B industrial brand with low consumer awareness, though known in clean fuels and trucking.

InterCloud is a company based in Paris, France, described by Crunchbase as the European leader of software-defined networking, listed under cloud computing and cloud infrastructure. That suggests it supplies connectivity and cloud networking services to businesses, though detailed products are not confirmed. It shows about $154 million in funding, with the latest round in February 2022. Ownership and scale cannot be verified from the available data, and it appears to be a B2B firm. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Mister Spex is a Berlin-based online optician selling glasses, contact lenses and sunglasses from many brands as well as its own labels, supported by physical stores in Germany and other European countries and online eye tests. Customers are consumers across Europe, and revenue is from product sales. Founded in 2007, it listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (MRX) in 2021. Recognisable consumer brand in German-speaking markets and parts of Europe in the eyewear sector.

Otrium is an Amsterdam-based online fashion outlet marketplace that lets premium and designer brands sell excess stock directly to shoppers at discounted prices, with the brands controlling their own pricing and assortment. Consumers use the site and app across Europe, and Otrium earns a commission and fees. Founded in 2017, it has raised about 133 million, with a 2021 round. Privately held. Growing consumer awareness in the Netherlands, Germany, France and neighbouring markets through online marketing.

Pomelo is a Buenos Aires fintech providing payments infrastructure in Latin America, with APIs that allow companies to issue cards, process payments and build financial products, including debit, credit and prepaid cards. Customers are fintechs, banks, retailers and other businesses, paying for card issuing and processing. Crunchbase shows about $157 million in funding, with the latest round in January 2026. Privately held. B2B, known within the regional fintech sector with no consumer awareness.

Poshmark is a social marketplace in which people buy and sell second-hand and new fashion, accessories and home items through an app and website, with the platform taking a commission on each sale and shipping labels provided. Based in Redwood City, California, it listed on Nasdaq (POSH) in January 2021 and was acquired by South Korea's Naver in a deal worth about $1.2 billion, completed in January 2023. It has millions of active users in the US, Canada, Australia and India. Well-known US consumer brand.

Progcap is a New Delhi fintech offering financing to small retailers and distributors in India, giving working capital to shopkeepers that buy from FMCG and consumer goods suppliers, using supply chain data to assess credit. It earns interest and fees on its loan book. Crunchbase shows about $151 million in funding, including debt facilities, with the latest round in October 2022. Privately held. B2B2C, known among small retailers and consumer goods brands in India, with little wider awareness.

Rive is a company based in Helsinki, Finland, which Crunchbase lists under artificial intelligence and describes as building what it calls the world's most accurate AI-powered real-something product, though the text is cut off, possibly real-estate or real-time related. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Sauce Labs is a San Francisco company offering cloud-based continuous testing for web and mobile applications, giving development teams access to thousands of real devices, browsers and operating systems to run automated and manual tests. Customers include large enterprises and software teams, who pay subscriptions. Founded in 2008, it has raised about $151 million, with backers such as Toba Capital and Riverwood. Privately held. B2B, well known to software testers and engineers, with no consumer awareness.

Sdui is a German school software company, based in Koblenz, with a digital communication and administration platform for schools, including apps for teachers, pupils and parents covering messaging, timetables, attendance and notices. Customers are schools, school authorities and education ministries, paying licence fees. Crunchbase shows about 139 million in funding, with the latest round in July 2025. Privately held. B2B2C, with solid recognition among German schools and parents, but little outside Germany.

ShadowBot (Yingdao) is a Hangzhou-based provider of robotic process automation software, offering software robots that perform repetitive office tasks such as data entry, reporting and web operations, and a low-code studio for building them. Customers are enterprises and small businesses in China, who pay licence and subscription fees. Crunchbase shows about $159 million raised, with the latest round in April 2022. Privately held. B2B, known in China's automation market and not among consumers.

Shippo is a San Francisco shipping platform with tools and APIs for small and mid-sized e-commerce sellers and marketplaces, covering label creation, rate comparison across carriers such as USPS, UPS, FedEx and DHL, tracking and returns. It earns subscription fees and a share of shipping spend. Founded in 2013, it has raised about $154 million. Privately held. B2B software serving hundreds of thousands of merchants, well known among online sellers but not a mainstream consumer brand.

Sift is a San Francisco company providing digital trust and safety software that uses machine learning, applied to a global network of data, to detect and prevent online fraud, including payment fraud, account takeover and abuse. Customers are online businesses such as marketplaces, fintechs and e-commerce brands, paying usage-based subscriptions. Founded in 2011, it has raised about $157 million, with investors including Insight Partners and Spark Capital. Privately held. B2B, recognised in fraud and risk circles with no consumer awareness.

The Lifetime Value Co. is a New York-based company described by Crunchbase as an online consumer and business-oriented operation, listed under data center and information-related categories. Trust Machines is a New York company building an ecosystem of applications and services around Bitcoin, including tools for Bitcoin layer-2 networks, wallets, staking and decentralised apps, and it is linked to the Stacks ecosystem and its founder Muneeb Ali. It earns from products, token-related activity and services. Crunchbase shows about $150 million raised, with a major round in February 2022. Privately held. Known among crypto and Bitcoin audiences, with little mainstream consumer recognition.

Voyageurs du Monde is a Paris-based travel group specialising in tailor-made and adventure trips, selling through its own agencies, website and specialist brands such as Terres d'Aventure and Comptoir des Voyages, as well as hotels and restaurants. Customers are French-speaking leisure travellers, and revenue is from package and trip margins. Founded in 1979, it is listed on Euronext Paris (VDM). Well-known name in the French travel market, with limited recognition abroad.

Wine.com is a San Francisco-based online wine retailer, shipping a large selection of wines and spirits to consumers in most US states, with a marketplace of partner merchants, a wine club and gift sales. It earns from product sales and delivery fees. Founded in 1998, it has raised about $156 million and is privately held. Among the best-known US online wine sellers, with consumer brand awareness built through e-commerce marketing and gifting seasons.

Zhichi Technologies is a Beijing-based provider of intelligent customer experience software, including AI chatbots, voice bots, customer service platforms and omnichannel contact centre tools, under its Sobot brand, used by businesses in China and overseas. Customers include e-commerce, finance, retail and internet firms, paying subscription and usage fees. Crunchbase shows about $155 million raised, with the latest round in February 2022. Privately held. B2B, with some recognition in Asian customer service software and no consumer brand awareness.

National Bank Holdings is a US bank holding company based in Greenwood Village, Colorado, operating NBH Bank, which provides commercial, small business and consumer banking, mortgages and wealth services across Colorado, Kansas, Missouri, Texas, Utah and New Mexico through branches, with some digital banking. It earns net interest income and fees. Listed on the NYSE (NBHC). Regional bank brand with recognition in its markets and little outside them.

Revelyst is a name that Crunchbase attaches here to a listing mentioning a renewable energy infrastructure company, Revera Energy, and a London, England location, alongside battery and energy categories. The record looks mixed, and it is also the name of a US outdoor products company that was separated from Vista Outdoor, so which firm is meant is unclear. It shows about $150 million in funding, with the latest round in February 2026. Treat as unverified. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Air Astana is the flag carrier of Kazakhstan, flying scheduled passenger and cargo services from its hubs in Almaty and Astana to destinations across Central Asia, Europe, the Middle East and Asia, and operating the low-cost carrier FlyArystan, with a fleet of around 40 or more Airbus and Boeing aircraft. It is owned by Samruk-Kazyna (51%) and BAE Systems (49%) before its 2024 IPO on the London Stock Exchange and Astana International Exchange (AIRA). Consumer airline brand known across the region.

Anaergia is a Canadian cleantech company, based in Burlington, Ontario, that builds and operates facilities converting organic waste, such as municipal and food waste, manure and wastewater sludge, into renewable natural gas, electricity, fertiliser and clean water. Customers are municipalities, utilities, farms and waste companies, with projects in North America, Europe and Asia. Revenue is from engineering and construction contracts, long-term operations and the sale of energy. Listed on the TSX (ANRG). B2B, with little consumer awareness.

b1BANK is a Louisiana community bank, headquartered in Baton Rouge, providing commercial, small business and personal banking, mortgages, treasury services and wealth management to customers through branches in Louisiana and Texas. It earns net interest income and fees. Crunchbase flags it as a listed company, with about $138 million in funding recorded in April 2026. Consumer recognition is regional, mainly in the Baton Rouge, New Orleans and Texas markets, and it has no national brand.

Flotek Industries is a Houston-based specialty chemistry and data analytics company. It makes chemistries for oil and gas drilling and completion, such as friction reducers and surfactants, serves energy producers and service companies, and operates the JP3 real-time fluid analysis service. It has also developed citrus-terpene based products. Revenue comes from chemical sales and data analytics subscriptions. Listed on the NYSE (FTK). B2B industrial brand with little consumer awareness; a $150 million funding event is shown in 2026.

Fly Exclusive is a private aviation company, based in Kinston, North Carolina, offering jet charter, fractional-style ownership programmes, aircraft management and maintenance, using a fleet of mid-size and light Citation business jets and its own maintenance operation. Customers are high-net-worth individuals and corporates. Revenue is from flight charges, management fees and maintenance. It went public via SPAC in 2023 and trades on NYSE American (FLYX). Niche premium aviation brand, well known to private jet buyers but not mass consumers.

Inseego is a San Diego company making wireless products for the 5G and 4G market, such as mobile hotspots, MiFi devices, fixed wireless access routers and indoor and outdoor 5G equipment, plus cloud management services for businesses and carriers. Customers are mobile operators such as Verizon and T-Mobile, enterprises, and consumers via carrier channels. Revenue is from hardware sales and subscriptions. Listed on Nasdaq (INSG). Brand recognition mainly with carriers and business buyers, and moderate among mobile hotspot users.

Lycos Energy is a Calgary-based oil and gas company producing heavy oil, mainly in the Lloydminster region of Alberta and Saskatchewan, and building its output through acquisitions and drilling. Customers are oil refiners and marketers, and revenue comes from selling crude oil. Crunchbase shows about $139 million in funding, with the latest round in July 2026, and it is publicly listed in Canada. Small energy producer, with no consumer brand awareness; fossil fuel exposure may matter for sponsorship fit.

NorthStar Earth & Space is a Montreal-based space data company, developing a constellation of satellites that track other satellites and debris, selling space situational awareness data to satellite operators, defence organisations and space agencies. Revenue would come from data subscriptions and services. Crunchbase shows about $149 million in funding, with the latest round in October 2026, and flags it as listed. It also has ties to Canadian and European space programmes. B2B and government, with little consumer awareness.

Silvergate Capital was the holding company of Silvergate Bank, based in La Jolla, California, a bank that became the main banking provider to the crypto industry through its Silvergate Exchange Network for transfers between exchanges and institutions. It was listed on the NYSE (SI), but after crypto exchange FTX collapsed in 2022 and deposits fled, it wound down and put the bank into voluntary liquidation in March 2023, with its shares delisted. Now defunct as a sponsor prospect.

88 Energy is an oil and gas exploration company listed on the ASX (88E), and the LSE earlier, headquartered in Subiaco, Western Australia. Its principal asset is the Project Phoenix acreage on the North Slope of Alaska, with interests in Peregrine and other prospects there. It is a junior explorer with no producing revenue of scale and relies on equity raises and partner funding. About AS$169 million shown in funding. B2B resource brand with no consumer awareness; fossil fuel exposure.

Abaxx Technologies is a Toronto-based financial technology and commodities exchange group, with Abaxx Exchange and Clearing in Singapore, which lists futures for physical commodities such as LNG, carbon, nickel sulphate and battery materials, and the Abaxx Commodity Services software business. Customers are traders, producers and financial institutions. It earns from exchange, clearing and software fees. Founded by Josephine Bush, it is listed in Canada and has raised about C$160 million. B2B with little consumer awareness.

Alliance Aviation Services is an Australian charter and wet-lease airline, based in Brisbane and listed on the ASX (AQZ), flying a fleet of Fokker and Embraer jets mainly for mining companies' fly-in fly-out workforces, and for airlines such as Qantas, Virgin Australia and Rex. It also maintains aircraft. Qantas moved to acquire the company from 2022. Sold mostly B2B, with little public consumer brand visibility, though its planes carry other airlines' livery.

BankFirst Financial Services is a Mississippi bank holding company, headquartered in Columbus, whose BankFirst Bank offers commercial, small business and personal banking, lending and mortgages through branches in Mississippi, Alabama and Tennessee. It earns net interest income and fees. Crunchbase shows about $103 million in funding, with the latest round in April 2026, and flags it as a listed company. Regional community bank brand, known locally and with no national consumer awareness.

Carver Federal Savings Bank, operating under Carver Bancorp (Nasdaq: CARV), is a New York bank based in Harlem, founded in 1948 as one of the largest black-owned banks in the United States. It provides personal and business banking, mortgages and commercial real estate lending through a handful of branches in New York City. It earns net interest income and fees and is a certified minority depository institution. Well-known community bank in Harlem and among minority-owned institutions, but small in scale.

Ceragon Networks is a wireless backhaul company, founded in Israel and listed on Nasdaq (CRNT), that makes microwave and millimetre-wave radio systems, 5G transport and private network solutions. Its US operations are based in Richardson, Texas, and Crunchbase lists the company there. Customers are mobile operators, utilities, governments and enterprises, buying equipment and services, and it has deployed networks in over 100 countries. B2B telecom equipment brand with little consumer recognition.

Dana Gas is a natural gas and related liquids producer based in Sharjah, in the United Arab Emirates, listed on the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange (DANA). It produces gas and condensate in Egypt and the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, and holds a stake in the Khor Mor field via Pearl Petroleum. Customers are state utilities and industrial buyers, with revenue from selling hydrocarbons. Regional B2B energy company with no consumer brand awareness; fossil fuel exposure.

Deep Fission is a Berkeley, California nuclear technology company developing small modular reactors that are installed deep in boreholes, about a mile underground, to supply low-cost carbon-free power, aimed at data centres and grid operators. It has no commercial reactors operating yet and funds itself through equity raises. Crunchbase shows about $114 million in funding, with the latest round in February 2026, and flags it as listed after a 2025 public-market entry. Early-stage energy brand, with little consumer awareness.

Draganfly is a Canadian drone company based in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, that develops and sells commercial and public-safety drones, software and services, including tactical and military drones for police, defence and first responders, and agriculture, public safety and inspection applications. Founded in 1998, it is listed on Nasdaq and the TSX (DPRO). Revenue is from drone sales, data services and contracts. B2B and government, with limited public awareness, though it is known in the drone community.

E3 Lithium is a Calgary-based lithium developer working on extracting lithium from brine in Alberta's Clearwater area, the Leduc formation, using its own direct lithium extraction technology, to supply battery makers. It has no commercial output yet and funds itself by equity raises and grants. Crunchbase shows about $118 million in funding, with the latest round in September 2026, and it is listed on the TSX Venture and Nasdaq. Early-stage mining and cleantech brand with no consumer awareness.

First Merchants is a US bank holding company, headquartered in Muncie, Indiana, operating First Merchants Bank, which offers commercial and consumer banking, wealth management, mortgages and insurance through branches in Indiana, Ohio, Michigan, Illinois and Wisconsin, with around $18 billion in assets. It earns net interest income and fees. Listed on Nasdaq (FRME). Strong regional community bank brand in the Midwest, with no national consumer profile.

Great Lakes Dredge & Dock is the largest US provider of dredging services, based in Oak Brook, Illinois, with contracts to deepen ports and channels, rebuild beaches and maintain waterways, mainly for the US Army Corps of Engineers, port authorities and offshore wind developers. It owns the biggest fleet of dredges in the country. Revenue is from government and private contracts. Listed on Nasdaq (GLDD). B2B and government, with no consumer awareness.

Gunnison Copper is a mining company based in Phoenix, Arizona, which operates and develops the Johnson Camp copper project in Cochise County, southeastern Arizona, and the Gunnison Copper project, using in-situ recovery to produce copper cathode. It sells copper to commodity buyers and funds itself through equity raises and offtake deals. Crunchbase shows about $97 million in funding, with the latest round in October 2026. It is listed on the TSX Venture. Junior miner, with no consumer awareness.

Haiki+ is an Italian circular economy company, based in Milan, active in recycling and waste management, collecting waste from industrial customers and producing recovered materials, plus services around sustainability and recovery. Customers are manufacturers and local administrations, paying for waste services, and it sells secondary raw materials. Crunchbase shows about 91 million in funding, with the latest round in April 2026, and flags it as listed, probably on Italy's Euronext Growth Milan. Small B2B environmental firm, little consumer brand awareness.

Happiest Minds Technologies is an Indian IT services and digital transformation company, founded in 2011 by Ashok Soota and based in Bengaluru, providing cloud, analytics, AI, cybersecurity, IoT and product engineering services to customers in banking, healthcare, retail, edtech and industrial sectors. It employs thousands of staff in India and offices in the US, UK and elsewhere. Revenue is from IT projects and managed services. Listed on the NSE and BSE since 2020. B2B, little consumer awareness.

High-Trend International Group is a company based in Singapore which Crunchbase lists under marine technology and marine-related industries, and flags as a listed company. The data suggest it supplies services or products for shipping or maritime use, though the details are not given in the source. It shows about $87 million in funding, with the latest round in May 2026. Customers, products, scale and listing venue cannot be confirmed from the available data. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

ideaForge is an Indian maker of unmanned aerial vehicles, based in Mumbai, supplying drones for surveillance, mapping and reconnaissance to the Indian armed forces, paramilitary and police, and to commercial users in mining, infrastructure and agriculture. Its drones, including the SWITCH UAV, are designed and built in India. Revenue comes from defence and commercial orders. Listed on the NSE and BSE since an IPO in July 2023. Well known in defence circles, with limited awareness among consumers.

Kneat is a Limerick, Ireland software company whose Kneat Gx platform digitises validation work in regulated industries, replacing paper and spreadsheets for equipment, process and cleaning validation in pharmaceutical and biotech manufacturing. Customers are drug makers and medical device firms, paying subscriptions. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (KSI). Founded in 2006, with offices in Europe and the US. B2B niche vendor, known in life sciences quality teams and with no consumer awareness.

Kruso Capital (Kruso Kapital) is a Milan-based Italian financial company that lends against and trades art, collectibles and other valuable assets, offering credit to owners and buyers of art, jewels and similar goods through its Kruso Art unit. Revenue is from interest, fees and sales. It is listed on Italy's Euronext Growth Milan market, and Crunchbase shows about 92 million in funding, with the latest round in September 2026. Niche financial brand, known with art collectors and dealers but little by the public.

Latitude Financial Services is an Australian consumer finance group, based in Melbourne, providing credit cards, personal loans, buy now pay later (GO Interest Free, Latitude Pay) and car loans, partly through retail partners such as Harvey Norman and other stores in Australia and New Zealand. It earns interest, fees and merchant revenue, and has millions of customer accounts. The business has its roots in GE Capital and is listed on the ASX (LFS). A 2023 cyberattack hit millions of records. Well known consumer finance brand in Australia.

LNG Energy Group is a Vancouver-based company which Crunchbase lists under chemical, energy and oil and gas, and flags as listed. The name suggests an LNG or natural gas business, but the source does not describe what it actually does or where it operates. It shows about $87 million in funding, with the latest round in May 2026. Its products, assets, customers and exchange cannot be confirmed from the available data. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

LT Foods is an Indian packaged foods group, based in Gurugram, best known for basmati rice brands including Daawat, Royal and Heritage, as well as organic foods, ready-to-eat meals and convenience foods. It sells in India and in more than 80 countries, to retailers and consumers, and earns from branded product sales. Founded in 1990 and listed on the NSE and BSE. Household name in India for premium basmati rice and well known in diaspora markets such as the US, Middle East and Europe.

Medallion Bank is a Utah-chartered industrial bank based in Salt Lake City, owned by Medallion Financial, which originates consumer loans for recreational vehicles, boats, motorcycles and home improvements, and funds them with deposits. It earns interest and fees. Preferred shares of Medallion Bank trade on Nasdaq. Crunchbase shows about $132 million in funding, with the latest round in September 2026. It operates through dealers and partners, so consumer awareness of the bank name itself is low.
