Verastem Oncology is a Needham, Massachusetts biopharma company listed on Nasdaq (VSTM), which received US approval in 2025 for Avmapki Fakzynja Co-pack (avutometinib and defactinib) for KRAS-mutated recurrent low-grade serous ovarian cancer, and is expanding into other RAS-pathway cancers. Revenue is just starting from product sales. Known in oncology and investor circles, with no consumer awareness. It is a small-cap company with a new commercial team, so its marketing spend is limited and aimed at oncologists, with sponsorship interest probably modest.

Zentalis Pharmaceuticals is a clinical stage oncology company, with offices in San Diego and Boston, listed on Nasdaq (ZNTL), developing azenosertib, a WEE1 inhibitor for cyclin E1-positive platinum-resistant ovarian cancer and other tumours. It has no approved products and is funded by equity raises and collaborations. Known in oncology and investor circles, with no consumer awareness. It is a small-cap company, so any marketing spend is limited and aimed at oncologists and investors, with sponsorship interest probably low.

Zoomlion is a major Chinese construction machinery maker, based in Changsha, Hunan, listed in Shenzhen and Hong Kong (1157), producing concrete machinery, mobile and tower cranes, earthmoving equipment, agricultural machines and aerial work platforms, sold to contractors worldwide. It is one of China's largest equipment makers, with overseas sales and a growing international presence. Revenue is from machinery sales and leasing. B2B industrial brand, with limited consumer awareness.

Zymeworks is a Vancouver-based biotech, now also with US operations, listed on Nasdaq (ZYME), which developed zanidatamab (Ziihera), a HER2 bispecific antibody approved in 2024 for biliary tract cancer and marketed by Jazz Pharmaceuticals, with Zymeworks earning royalties and milestones. It also has a pipeline of antibody drug conjugates. Known in oncology and investor circles, with no consumer awareness. It is a small-cap company with several hundred staff, so any marketing spend is limited and aimed at investors and oncologists.

Allete is a Duluth, Minnesota energy company that owns Minnesota Power, a regulated electric utility serving northern Minnesota, with a fast-growing share of renewable energy, plus ALLETE Clean Energy, BNI Energy coal mine and real estate holdings. It was listed on the NYSE (ALE) and was agreed in 2024 to be taken private by CPP Investments and Global Infrastructure Partners. Revenue is from regulated utility rates and contracts with industrial customers. Regional utility brand, with no national profile.

Godrej Properties is one of India's largest listed real estate developers, based in Mumbai and part of the Godrej Group, developing residential apartments, townhouses and commercial projects in cities including Mumbai, Delhi NCR, Pune and Bengaluru. Revenue is from property sales. Listed on the NSE and BSE. Crunchbase shows about INR 60 billion in funding, with the latest round in November 2024. Strong consumer brand in Indian property, supported by the trusted Godrej name.

Lincoln Property Company is a US real estate developer, owner and manager, based in Dallas, active in multifamily apartments, commercial offices, retail and mixed-use projects across the United States and Europe, with a large third-party management business. The record also mentions a project with Austin Capital Partners, but the details are cut off. Crunchbase shows about $870 million in funding, with the latest round in June 2026. Privately held. Recognised in the property industry, with limited awareness among consumers.

Maritime Partners is a Metairie, Louisiana company that owns and leases inland barges and towboats to operators on US rivers and waterways, serving shippers of grain, chemicals, petroleum and other bulk cargoes. Revenue comes from leasing fleets under long-term contracts. Crunchbase shows about $750 million in funding, with the latest round in November 2024. Privately held. B2B transport asset brand, with no consumer awareness.

MITER Brands is a US manufacturer of residential windows and doors, formed by combining MI Windows and Doors and Milgard, with brands including Milgard, MI Windows and Doors, and Fibertec. It sells through dealers, distributors and home centres to builders and homeowners. Crunchbase shows a Fife, Washington location, which matches Milgard's base, and about $700 million in funding, with the latest round in March 2024. Privately held. Known in the building trades, with moderate homeowner recognition.

Newease China is a company based in Shanghai, China, described by Crunchbase as a leading investor and operator of hubs, listed under logistics and warehousing. That suggests logistics real estate or distribution hubs, but the source text is cut off. It shows about $800 million in funding, with the latest round in September 2018. Its customers, ownership and size cannot be confirmed from the available data. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Panattoni is one of the world's largest private industrial real estate developers, founded in 1986 in California by Carl Panattoni, which builds warehouses, logistics parks and manufacturing facilities for tenants such as Amazon and DHL, with major activity in Europe, especially Poland, Germany and the UK, plus the US. Revenue is from development and sales. Crunchbase shows a London address and about 625 million in funding, latest in September 2024. Known in the property and logistics industry, not to consumers.

Parsons Corporation is a Chantilly, Virginia engineering, technology and construction company, listed on the NYSE (PSN), providing services for defence, intelligence, cyber, space and critical infrastructure, such as transport projects, to government and commercial customers. It employs around 18,000 people and was founded in 1944. Revenue is from government and project contracts. B2B and government brand, well known in defence and infrastructure circles, with no consumer awareness.

PulteGroup is one of the largest US homebuilders, based in Atlanta and listed on the NYSE (PHM), building and selling homes under the Pulte Homes, Centex, Del Webb (active adult communities), DiVosta and John Wieland brands, as well as providing mortgage and title services. It builds in around 45 US markets. Revenue is from home sales, around $17 billion a year. Strong consumer brand in US housing, with a local sponsorship tradition.

The AZEK Company is a Chicago-based maker of outdoor living products, mainly TimberTech composite and PVC decking, railing, AZEK Exteriors trim and mouldings, and StruXure pergolas, sold through dealers and distributors to homeowners, builders and contractors. It was listed on the NYSE (AZEK) and acquired by James Hardie in 2025 for about $8.75 billion. Revenue was about $1.4 billion a year. Recognised in residential building products and by homeowners planning decks.

The ODP Corporation is a Boca Raton, Florida business-to-business and consumer distributor of office products and supplies, owning Office Depot and OfficeMax retail stores, ODP Business Solutions and the supply chain unit Veyer. It serves businesses, schools, governments and consumers. It was listed on Nasdaq (ODP) and was acquired by Atlas Holdings in 2025 in a take-private deal valued at about $1 billion. Strong consumer brand awareness in the US, with a large retail footprint.

XPO is a Greenwich, Connecticut freight transportation company listed on the NYSE (XPO), now focused on less-than-truckload (LTL) freight in North America, with a network of terminals and trucks, after spinning off GXO Logistics and RXO in 2021. Customers are industrial, retail and commercial shippers, and revenue is from freight charges. Founded by Brad Jacobs. B2B logistics brand, known to shippers and drivers, with limited consumer awareness.

Arcosa is a Dallas company, spun off from Trinity Industries in 2018 and listed on the NYSE (ACA), which makes infrastructure-related products: construction aggregates, engineered structures (utility poles, wind towers), steel components and storage tanks. Customers are construction, utility, transportation and energy firms, and revenue is about $2.5 billion a year. B2B industrial brand, known in construction and infrastructure industries, with no consumer awareness.

Canary Wharf Group is the developer, owner and manager of Canary Wharf, the London financial district on the Isle of Dogs, with offices, shops, restaurants, apartments and the Elizabeth line station, home to banks such as HSBC, Barclays and Citi. Owned by Brookfield and the Qatar Investment Authority, through the Songbird structure. Revenue is rents from tenants. Crunchbase shows about $561 million in funding, latest in December 2024. Famous London landmark and destination, with strong brand visibility.

InterDigital is a Wilmington, Delaware research and licensing company, listed on Nasdaq (IDCC), which develops wireless and video technologies and licenses its patent portfolio to smartphone, TV, PC and other device makers, including Apple and Samsung. Revenue is from patent licence fees and royalties, over $500 million a year. Funding of about $675 million is recorded, latest in 2019. B2B technology licensing brand, with no consumer awareness.

Landsea Homes is a US homebuilder, with a Crunchbase location of Dallas, Texas, and a main base in Newport Beach, California, listed on Nasdaq (LSEA), which builds single-family homes, townhomes and condominiums in Arizona, California, Texas, Florida, the Northeast and other states. Revenue is from home sales, around $1.5 billion a year. It was formed via a SPAC merger in 2021 and has Chinese parent roots. Local consumer homebuilder brand with regional recognition.

LD Celulose is a dissolving wood pulp producer with a mill at Indianopolis in Minas Gerais, Brazil, which is a joint venture between Austria's Lenzing and Brazil's Duratex (now Dexco). The pulp is used for textile fibres such as viscose and lyocell. The mill began operating in 2022, with capacity of around 500,000 tonnes a year, and the project cost about $1.3 billion. Revenue is from selling pulp to fibre makers. B2B industrial brand, with no consumer awareness.

Mobiliare Real Estate Solutions is a Guatemala City company, described by Crunchbase as a real estate investment fund, and listed under property management. It appears to operate in real estate in Guatemala, but the source gives no detail about its properties or investors. It shows about $600 million in funding, with the latest round in June 2026. Its ownership, size and track record cannot be confirmed from the available data. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Plymouth Industrial REIT is a Boston-based real estate investment trust listed on the NYSE (PLYM), which owns and operates industrial properties such as warehouses and distribution centres, mainly in secondary markets in the US Midwest, Southeast and Northeast, with leases to logistics and manufacturing tenants. Revenue is rent. Funding of $600 million is recorded, with the latest in November 2024. B2B property brand, with no consumer awareness.

Prestige Group is a major Indian real estate developer, based in Bengaluru, whose listed arm Prestige Estates Projects builds residential apartments, offices, retail malls and hotels, mainly in Bengaluru, Mumbai, Hyderabad and Chennai. Founded in 1986, it is listed on the NSE and BSE. Crunchbase shows about INR 50 billion in funding, with the latest round in September 2024. Strong consumer brand in South Indian housing, with a large presence in property advertising.

Purchasing Power is an Atlanta company that offers employee purchase programmes, letting workers buy products such as electronics, appliances and furniture through payroll deduction, and which has also moved into financial wellness services such as emergency savings. Its customers are employers, with employees as end users, and revenue is from product margins and fees. Crunchbase shows about $620 million in funding, with the latest round in March 2026. Privately held. Known in the HR benefits market, with limited public awareness.

Red Lobster is a US casual dining chain, based in Orlando, Florida, known for seafood such as Cheddar Bay Biscuits, shrimp and lobster, with about 500 restaurants in the US and Canada. It was owned by Darden, then Golden Gate Capital, then Thai Union, and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in May 2024 after losses, emerging in September 2024 owned by its lenders led by Fortress. Revenue is from restaurant sales. Household consumer brand across the US.

Shufersal is Israel's largest supermarket and retail chain, based in Rishon LeZion, with hundreds of stores under formats including Shufersal Deal, Sheli, Yesh and Online, plus the Be pharmacy chain and a loyalty club of millions of members. Revenue is from grocery and pharmacy sales. It is listed on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (SHUF). Strong consumer brand in Israel, with no presence abroad.

Transportation Equipment Network is a company based in Dublin, Ohio, listed by Crunchbase under leasing, rental and transportation, with the short description saying it offers industry-specific services, cut off in the source. It appears to deal in trucks, trailers or transport equipment rental and leasing, but this is not confirmed. It shows about $600 million in funding, with the latest round in July 2024. Its customers, ownership and size cannot be verified. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Trinity Industries is a Dallas-based railcar leasing and manufacturing company, listed on the NYSE (TRN), whose TrinityRail unit owns and leases a fleet of roughly 100,000 railcars, and builds tank and freight cars for shippers, railroads and lessors. Revenue is from leasing and railcar sales. It spun off Arcosa in 2018. Funding of $600 million is recorded, with the latest in May 2024. B2B industrial brand, known in rail freight, with no consumer awareness.

Wienerberger is a Vienna-based international building materials group, listed on the Vienna Stock Exchange (WIE), and one of the world's largest brick makers. It produces clay blocks (Porotherm), facing bricks (Terca), roof tiles (Koramic), concrete pavers (Semmelrock) and plastic and ceramic pipes (Pipelife), with plants in about 30 countries. Customers are builders, contractors and distributors. Founded in 1819. B2B brand with some consumer recognition in European home building.
